# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: Stops the source generator and the MsgPack00x analyzer from crashing when a `[MessagePackObject]` member's type is a closed generic struct defined in a referenced assembly. Two diagnostic paths in `TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo` indexed `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`, which is empty for metadata symbols. They now use null-safe lookups (lines 985, 1077, plus a new helper at 1434). Separately, every diagnostic the analyzer reports through `TypeCollector` now goes through a wrapper (239, 1444-1450). The wrapper drops any diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the current compilation. Three new tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata-only image and then check two things: no diagnostics from the verifier, and a resolver hint name in the generator's output. README and MsgPack004.md gain paragraphs describing the new behaviour.
story.why: REQ-2283 asks for a clean build and a generated resolver when a closed generic value type comes from a referenced assembly. Today the generator throws and silently emits no resolver.
touches_beyond_requirement: The diagnostic filter at TypeCollector.cs 239/1444-1450 applies to every analyzer diagnostic, not only the two crash sites. It silently drops any diagnostic whose location is Location.None, including ones about the user's own source types where a location helper returns null.
New documentation in README.md (1639-1643) and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md (48-52) promising that diagnostics for referenced types are reported by the defining assembly.
story.confidence_overview: Medium. Line 1077 is evaluated unconditionally on the ternary path, and the old code indexed [0] there, so the switch to FirstOrDefault plausibly removes the generator crash. The tests reproduce the issue's record-struct case with a real metadata reference and assert that a resolver is generated. The issue names three [0] indexing sites, but only two are visibly changed; I cannot see whether the third (issue's line 735) was already safe or is unreachable. I also cannot confirm that VerifyCS.Test runs the MsgPack00x analyzer, so the AD0001 half of the fix is less certain than the CS8785 half.

refusals.what: A global filter silently suppresses every analyzer diagnostic whose location is not in the current compilation, including Location.None diagnostics on the user's own source types.
refusals.why: This is a user-visible change in analyzer behaviour beyond fixing the crash. A human should decide whether swallowing diagnostics, rather than reporting them at Location.None or at the referencing member, is acceptable.

refusals.what: New documentation promises a policy (diagnostics for referenced types are reported only by the defining assembly) that the requirement did not ask for.
refusals.why: These docs codify a design decision introduced by this change, not by the requirement.

refusals.what: README section documenting the same new diagnostics policy and support claim.
refusals.why: Beyond the requirement. It states support (including generic record structs) that the tests verify only to the extent of producing a resolver hint name.

findings.description: The filter drops every diagnostic whose location is Location.None, not only those for metadata symbols. Any TypeCollector diagnostic about a source type whose location helper returns null is now silently swallowed. Examples are GetPropertyIdentifierLocation on a positional record property, where the syntax is a ParameterSyntax rather than a PropertyDeclarationSyntax, and GetIdentifierLocation or GetParameterListLocation returning null. Users would get no warning where previously there was a diagnostic or an exception.

For a record positional property (`[property: Key(...)]` on a primary constructor parameter), DeclaringSyntaxReferences yields a ParameterSyntax. The `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax` cast returns null, so BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull on the user's own positional record now gets no location and is then dropped by the filter at 1446.

The issue lists three `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (its lines 735, 1009, 1101). Only two are visibly changed (985, 1077). The site corresponding to the issue's line 735 (around new line 710) is not in the diff, so it is unclear whether it is still reachable for metadata types and could still crash on other shapes.

The AD0001 half of the fix depends on VerifyCS.Test (CSharpSourceGeneratorVerifier) actually running MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer. The diff does not show that. If it only runs the generator, the analyzer crash path is untested; the direct driver run at 653-656 covers only the generator.

The tests check only that a resolver hint name exists. They do not check that the resolver can serialize `Item<int>` at runtime. The defining assembly is compiled without the generator, so no formatter for Item<T> exists anywhere. Trimmed/AOT behaviour, which the issue cites as the real impact, is not verified.

The claim that diagnostics are 'reported by the assembly that defines it' holds only if the defining assembly also runs the MessagePack analyzer. For third-party NuGet types, such diagnostics are now never surfaced.

The true branch of the same ternary fixed on line 1077 still evaluates derivedKeyAttribute.GetSyntax(this.cancellationToken).GetLocation() unconditionally (even for private members and even when reportDiagnostic is null in the generator). If a closed generic [MessagePackObject] type from a referenced assembly has a member with an attribute deriving from KeyAttribute or IgnoreMemberAttribute, its metadata AttributeData has no syntax (ApplicationSyntaxReference is null), throwing NullReferenceException and crashing both MessagePackGenerator (CS8785, silently omitting the consuming assembly's resolver) and MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer (AD0001).

GetPropertyIdentifierLocation casts the syntax node with 'as PropertyDeclarationSyntax', which returns null for synthesized properties of positional records and record structs declared in source in the current compilation (whose DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] is a ParameterSyntax, e.g., record Cmd([property: Key(null!)] string Scope)). Because a null location becomes Location.None (IsInSource == false), ReportIfLocatedInCompilation on line 1446 treats the diagnostic as external and silently drops BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull for positional records in the project being compiled.

out_of_scope.description: New user-facing documentation section about generic types from referenced assemblies and where their diagnostics are reported.
New documentation section stating that the analyzer skips members of referenced types.
The global diagnostic filter (239, 1444-1450) changes reporting for all TypeCollector diagnostics, beyond the null-safe indexing the issue asked for.
